name: Toyota 2JZ-GE, first generation without VVT-i (1991-1997; JZA80 Supra non-turbo, Aristo/GS 300, SC 300)
summary: Square 3.0 L iron-block straight-six with mild cams, a two-stage (ACIS) plenum intake and two cast-iron three-cylinder exhaust manifolds; smooth, even-firing six-cylinder note with a modest rev range.

bore_mm.note: Toyota service spec for the cylinder bore: 86.000-86.013 mm (https://www.toyota-supra.de/repair-manual/a80/service-specifications/engine-mechanical-2jz-ge).

compression_ratio.note: Non-VVT-i engine. The VVT-i engine is 10.5:1.

firing_order.note: Also given by https://tractortechspecs.com/toyota_2jz_ge_specs.html. Neither page states the numbering convention; single bank.

crank.note: Pin angles not stated. Main journal 61.984-62.000 mm, crank pin 51.982-52.000 mm per the Supra repair manual.

valves_per_cylinder.note: DOHC, belt drive, direct-acting buckets with outer shims; 45 degree included valve angle.

intake_lift_mm.note: Cam lobe height per the Supra repair manual: 44.570-44.670 mm intake.

exhaust_lift_mm.note: Cam lobe height: 44.770-44.870 mm exhaust per https://tractortechspecs.com/toyota_2jz_ge_specs.html.

intake_duration_deg.note: Lift at which this is measured is not stated; it equals the sum of the open and close events below, so it is the same (unknown) basis.

exhaust_duration_deg.note: Lift basis not stated. VVT-i engine: 226 deg.

evc_atdc.note: Measuring lift not stated. Overlap 6 deg.

idle_rpm.note: 700 +/- 50 rpm, Supra (A80) repair manual service specifications. A 1997 Supra manual copy lists 700 +/- 50 in one table and 650 +/- 50 in another (https://personal.tcu.edu/blucas/carstuff/supra/misc/Supra1997Manual/Torque%20&%20Service%20Specifications.pdf).

peak_power_kw.note: 220 PS at 5800 rpm, the lowest of the non-VVT-i ratings listed; the same page lists up to 230 PS (169 kW) at 6000 rpm depending on market and model. Wikipedia gives a 215-230 PS range across all 2JZ-GE versions.

peak_torque_nm.note: Non-VVT-i range on the page: 279 to 284 Nm at 4800 rpm.

intake_type.value: plenum, single throttle body, with ACIS: a bulkhead divides the manifold and an intake air control valve opens to change the effective intake length with engine speed and throttle opening

header_type.value: two cast-iron exhaust manifolds (dual), joining into a centre pipe that splits into a Y with a sub-muffler on each branch
header_type.note: The VVT-i engine changed to stainless manifolds with longer branches.

missing: rod_length_mm (142 mm appears on aftermarket rod listings seen only in search snippets; no page stating the factory length was opened)
the lift at which Toyota's valve timing and duration are measured
runner_length_mm and runner_dia_mm, and the ACIS switch rpm
which cylinders feed which exhaust manifold (1-3 and 4-6 assumed by convention, not stated)

sources.what: Australian Car Reviews technical article on the 2JZ-GE: block, head, valve sizes and lift, valve timing tables for non-VVT-i and VVT-i, intake (ACIS), exhaust, firing order. Detailed secondary source that reads like a digest of Toyota's new-car features documents; no primary citation given.
Online copy of the Toyota Supra (A80) repair manual service specifications for the 2JZ-GE: idle speed, cam lobe height, bore, journal diameters.
PDF copy of the 1997 Toyota Supra repair manual torque and service specifications; cross-check for idle speed.
Third-party spec page: power and torque ratings by version, firing order, valve and cam lobe dimensions. Secondary; figures agree with the two sources above where they overlap.
Wikipedia JZ article: variant overview and output range.

vehicle.name: Toyota Supra non-turbo five-speed (JZA80, US, 1993)

curb_kg.note: 'Transmission five speed manual w/od Curb Weight 3260'; converted by me (1478.7 kg). Standard not stated. Toyota Japan's catalogue gives the JDM SZ 5-speed as '車両重量 1410kg' (https://toyota.jp/ucar/catalog/brand-TOYOTA/car-SUPRA/199305/1000911/), a different market.

gears.note: Wikipedia (cross-check grade, no Toyota document found): W58 'First Gear: 3.285:1 Second Gear: 1.894:1 Third Gear: 1.275:1 Fourth Gear: 1.00:1 Fifth Gear: 0.783:1 Reverse: 3.768:1', applications '1993–1998 Toyota Supra (A80) non-turbo'.

final_drive.note: Grannas Racing differential table, US spec: '1993-1996 A05A 4.272 OPEN', '1993-1996 A05B 4.272 LSD' (not split by gearbox). Tuner source. 1997-98 cars used 4.083 or 3.769. The JDM SZ 5-speed is 4.083 per Toyota Japan.

wheel_radius_m.note: Calculated by me from the tyre size 245/50 ZR16 (rim diameter / 2 + section width x aspect ratio): unloaded geometric radius, not a published rolling radius.

tyre.note: 'Tires Goodyear Eagle GS-C Front: P225/50ZR16 Rear: P245/50ZR16'. Rear (driven) size used.

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'Toyota Supra' (read 2026-11-17), infobox layout: Front-engine, rear-wheel-drive.

missing: Toyota source for the gear ratios and final drive

sources.what: The Auto Channel, period review of the 1993 Toyota Supra non-turbo (base price $33,900, 220 hp at 5800 rpm, five-speed manual): curb weight and tyres.
Wikipedia, Toyota W transmission: W58 ratios and applications. Cross-check grade; used because no Toyota document was found.
Grannas Racing (Supra tuner), Supra Mk IV differential codes and ratios by year and market.
Toyota Japan used-car catalogue, Supra SZ 5MT (E-JZA80, May 1993): JDM weight and final drive. Different market; cross-check.
